title: Concurrency Control for Session Storage
description:
Add concurrency protection to oboe-mcp/oboe-cli session storage. Session state is flat JSON (session_*.json + index.json) mutated by naive read-modify-write with no locking and no atomic writes, so concurrent MCP/CLI access can lose updates, truncate files mid-read, and desynchronize the index. Full analysis and risk inventory: docs/concurrency-handoff.md (committed 374d84a).

Design decisions already taken (2026-07-31): retry strategy is caller-selectable — block (default, optional timeout) or fail-fast; read paths acquire locks, and a read feeding a write holds its lock across the whole read-modify-write cycle. Constraints: no new runtime dependencies (fcntl.flock on POSIX), session file format must not change.

items.title: Decide lock granularity and shared-vs-exclusive read mode
items.description: Per-session-file lock plus a separate lock for index.json (every mutation touches both). Open sub-question: should the read path take a shared lock (fcntl LOCK_SH) so concurrent readers do not block each other, or exclusive for simplicity? Blocks the implementation items.
items.resolution: CHANGED from the proposed per-file plan: one lock per sessions directory, not per session file plus a separate index lock. Reading the code showed the split buys nothing — every mutation writes index.json, so the index lock already serializes all writers, while per-file locks would add a deadlock hazard via create_child_session. Reads take a shared lock (fcntl LOCK_SH) so concurrent readers still run in parallel.

items.title: Define a single documented lock acquisition order
items.description: create_child_session locks the parent, then creates the child (which locks the child and updates the index). Without one consistent global order, two processes creating reciprocal children can deadlock. Decide and document the order (proposal: session files by sorted filename, then index.json last).
items.resolution: Moot under the single-directory lock: there is only one lock, so no ordering exists to get wrong. create_child_session / complete_child_session nest into the lock the outer operation already holds. Re-entrancy is per-thread and depth-counted; escalating a held shared lock to exclusive raises ValueError rather than silently releasing mid-operation. Covered by test_lock_is_reentrant_within_a_process and test_composite_operation_holds_one_lock_throughout.

items.title: Decide default timeout for blocking mode
items.description: Dr. Greg chose block-by-default with an optional timeout. Decide whether block-with-no-timeout waits forever (risking a wedged agent on a stale lock) or falls back to a generous built-in ceiling that raises a clear error.
items.resolution: 30s finite ceiling (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT), not an unbounded wait. An indefinite wait on a lock left by a wedged process gives the caller no diagnostic and no way out; the timeout error names the lock file and its recorded holder (pid/host/time). Indefinite waiting remains available on request via --lock-timeout none / OBOE_LOCK_TIMEOUT=none.

items.title: Decide non-POSIX fallback behavior
items.description: fcntl.flock is POSIX-only. Decide between a msvcrt-based Windows path, a lockfile-based portable fallback, or a documented no-op with a warning. A silent no-op on Windows would give users a false guarantee, so this needs an explicit decision.
items.resolution: Portable O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile fallback, not a no-op. It cannot express shared mode, so readers are serialized there — surfaced honestly via supports_shared_locks() and reported by oboe_get_lock_policy as concurrent_readers:false, rather than letting callers assume a guarantee they do not have. The fallback reaps a lockfile whose owning PID no longer exists, so a crash cannot wedge a directory permanently. Note: the fallback path is untested on real Windows — no CI runner available; POSIX path is the one exercised.

items.title: Implement atomic writes in save_session and _save_index
items.description: Both currently open with mode 'w', truncating immediately (session.py:110 and session.py:237). Replace with write-to-temp-file-then-os.replace so a concurrent reader never observes a truncated or partial file. Addresses risk 2 (truncation race).
items.resolution: atomic_write_json() in the new locking.py: mkstemp in the same directory, json.dump, flush, fsync, os.replace. Both save_session and _save_index now route through it. Verified by negative control — reverting to open(...,"w") makes test_atomic_write_never_exposes_partial_file fail with JSONDecodeError, which is risk 2 reproducing exactly.

items.title: Implement the lock primitive with block/timeout/fail-fast
items.description: A context manager wrapping fcntl.flock exposing the caller-selectable policy: block (default) with an optional timeout, or fail-fast raising immediately when held. No new runtime dependencies.
items.resolution: sessions_lock() context manager in locking.py, with LockPolicy(blocking, timeout) and the LockError/LockBusy/LockTimeout hierarchy. fcntl.flock with LOCK_NB in a backoff poll loop gives flock a timeout it does not natively have. No new runtime dependencies — pyproject still declares only mcp>=2.0,<3.

items.title: Make read paths acquire locks
items.description: load_session, list_sessions, and the other read entry points must acquire a lock rather than reading unsynchronized. A read that feeds a subsequent write holds its lock across the whole read-modify-write cycle rather than releasing and re-acquiring.
items.resolution: load_session and load_index take a shared lock; list_sessions holds one across the index read and escalates to exclusive only for the rebuild-repair path. session_status, get_next, list_items and get_item inherit protection through load_session. Reads feeding writes hold the exclusive lock for the whole cycle via session_transaction rather than releasing and re-acquiring. Unlocked _load_session_unlocked / _load_index_unlocked variants exist for use inside a held lock. Verified by test_readers_do_not_block_each_other and test_writer_waits_for_reader.

items.title: Wrap all mutation functions in session+index transactions
items.description: Every function calling save_session followed by _upsert_index needs both writes under held locks so the pair is consistent: mark_complete, mark_skip, mark_deferred, mark_blocked, mark_in_progress, complete_session, cancel_session, create_child_session, complete_child_session, merge_items, set_approval, update_field, create_session, trim_sessions. Addresses risks 1, 3, 4, 6.
items.resolution: session_transaction() wraps all 12 simple mutations (mark_complete, mark_skip, mark_deferred, mark_blocked, mark_in_progress, complete_session, cancel_session, merge_items, set_approval, update_field). create_session performs its exists() check inside the lock, closing the TOCTOU. trim_sessions decides-and-deletes atomically. create_child_session and complete_child_session hold one lock across both files. An exception inside a transaction aborts the write entirely. Grepped for the old save_session+_upsert_index pattern afterwards: zero remaining sites.

items.title: Plumb the lock policy through the MCP and CLI surfaces
items.description: The calling agent selects block-vs-fail-fast, so the choice must be reachable from both transports: a parameter on the MCP tools and a flag on oboe-cli, with the documented default. Includes deciding whether it is per-call or per-connection.
items.resolution: Per-connection/per-process, not per-call — adding a parameter to all 20 existing tools would have been invasive for a setting that rarely changes mid-session. MCP: new oboe_set_lock_policy / oboe_get_lock_policy tools (server now has 22, docstring updated). CLI: --lock-timeout / --lock-fail-fast global flags. Environment: OBOE_LOCK_POLICY / OBOE_LOCK_TIMEOUT. LockError added to the server's _TOOL_EXCEPTIONS tuple, which covers all 19 handler sites at once so contention reaches agents as a normal tool error rather than an unhandled exception.

items.title: Add concurrency regression tests
items.description: Per the verification criteria: parallel completes on different items in one session must not lose updates; parallel CLI plus MCP operations must not corrupt data; index.json must stay consistent under concurrent load; all existing single-process tests must still pass. Needs real multi-process tests, not just threads, since the protection is process-level.
items.resolution: tests/test_concurrency.py — 18 tests using real subprocesses (threads would exercise re-entrancy, not the cross-process protection). Covers all four verification criteria plus policy behaviour and the CLI/MCP surfaces. Total suite 281 passing; the 263 pre-existing tests still pass, with one over-broad assertion in test_cli.py corrected (it counted every file in the sessions dir, now globs session_*.json). Validated by negative control: with locking no-op'd and the atomic write reverted, 10 of 14 core concurrency tests fail — so they genuinely detect the bugs rather than merely passing.

items.title: Document the concurrency contract for agents
items.description: Record the guarantees, the lock policy options and default, the acquisition order, and the non-POSIX caveat in README/SKILL.md so calling agents know what they get and which failure they must handle when using fail-fast.
items.resolution: New "Concurrency" section in README.md covering the guarantees, the policy table across all three surfaces (MCP/CLI/env), the finite-default rationale, and the non-POSIX serialized-readers caveat. docs/concurrency-handoff.md updated with the as-built design, the granularity change and its reasoning, and the negative-control result. Not done: SKILL.md — the repo has no SKILL.md; the agent-facing skill lives in agent-config, so updating it is a separate change outside this repo.
